dedupe_keys.name: life adapt island coral mangrove and seagrass restoration guadeloupe

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the LIFE Adapt'Island project (July 2019 to June 2024) led by the Grand Port Maritime de la Guadeloupe with Pilot4Dev and France Nature Environnement Guadeloupe, which restored coral reefs, mangrove and swamp forests and seagrass meadows in the industrial zones of Jarry and Petit-Cul-de-Sac Marin and at Folle-Anse on Marie-Galante, to strengthen Guadeloupe's natural coastal defences against storms, erosion and sea level rise. IFREMER data cited show coral cover on windward reefs falling from 30 percent in 2007 to 15 percent in 2019. Coral fragments of Acropora and other species were grown in two nurseries near Caye à Dupont and transplanted in 2021, 2022 and 2023, with spawning collection as a second technique; mangrove nurseries were set up by 2022, and seagrass was protected with screw-anchor moorings in 2023 and replanted in early 2024. Society actions included an underwater seagrass trail, posters and television campaigns. The EU contribution was about 2.53 million euros. The page, published in December 2024 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the Cayoli and LIFE pages. Caveats: early survival of seagrass and coral transplants was low because of moorings, storms and disease, and outcomes depend on long-term monitoring. It illustrates nature-based coastal hazard reduction and climate adaptation around port infrastructure; related records are the Allen Coral Atlas and Global Mangrove Watch.
name: LIFE Adapt'Island coral, mangrove and seagrass restoration (Guadeloupe)
organisations: Grand Port Maritime de la Guadeloupe
outcomes: Corals were transplanted yearly in 2021-2023, mangrove nurseries established and seagrass moorings and replanting completed, though early transplant survival was low.
